newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends slightly lower on uncertain weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends slightly lower on uncertain weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed slightly lower in choppy dealings which reflected uncertainty about weather patterns in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Early Friday there were some private forecasts which indicated a more conducive weather pattern over the near term in the Midwest for pollination of the U.S. corn crop.
Temperatures above 90 degrees Fahrenheit were expected this weekend in the Midwest but meteorologists said a cold front would move in by Monday, bringing temperatures back to normal.

"The next couple of days for at least the western and southern Corn Belt will be the hottest weather of the summer so far," said Craig Solberg, Freese-Notis meteorologist. "We're becoming less optimistic about the rainfall."
Joel Burrgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist said 0.25 to 1.00 inch of rain would be the norm in the Midwest with 40 to 60 percent coverage.
Corn closed unchanged to 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1/4 at $2.43-1/4. December was down 3/4 at $2.43-1/4.
In spread dealings, Cargill Inc did nearly one million bushels of September/December at 3/4 cent, premium September, traders said.

Tenco Inc bought five million bushels of December and sold three million December, traders said. Griffin Trading, ING Derivatives and Rand Financial each bought two million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000 contracts, above the 43,868 traded Thursday.

In corn options, E.D. and F. Man International bought 600 December $2.50 calls at 10 cents, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 500 December $2.40 puts at 9-3/4 cents and sold 1,000 December $2.30 puts at 5-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 16,787 traded Thursday.
